newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Five major Albanian towns in rebel hands-reports.
newsitem.headline: Five major Albanian towns in rebel hands-reports.

text.p: At least five major towns in southwestern Albania are reported to be in the hands of rebels who refuse to surrender weapons despite a political accord signed at the weekend by President Sali Berisha and 10 political parties.
Here is the situation in southern Albania as of midday (1100 GMT) on Monday, according to reports received from the region.

- Vlore. Albania's second largest Adriatic port, effectively seized in early February by residents furious at the loss of their savings in the failed Gjallica pyramid investment scheme. The town of 80,000 came under control of more organised armed rebels on February 28 after a confrontation between protesters and secret police.

- Sarande. Smaller port and resort town further south, opposite the Greek holiday island of Corfu. Ferries travel regularly the short distance to the island. The town, with a population of about 15,000, is one of the centres for Albania's ethnic Greek community. It came under firm control of insurgents after Vlore.
- Delvine. Sixteen km (10 miles) inland from Sarande. A small town which fell to the rebels in the same wave that brought the two ports under insurgent control.

- Tepelene. A remote mountain town of 20,000 on the main national road south to Greece. It is the site of a top-security prison which held Socialist party leader Fatos Nano, jailed on corruption charges in 1994. He was moved to Tirana before the insurgents took control of the town last week and set up big artillery guns in the central square.

- Gjirokaster. An ancient town and centre of the ethnic Greek community, only 30 km (20 miles) from the Greek border. Rebels overran the town and raided a big military barracks on Saturday after a government attempt to fly in troop reinforcements. President Berisha and the opposition have pointedly said the Greek community has no direct connection with the insurgents.
- Permet. Town in one of Albania's most remote districts. Rebels took control of it on Sunday before the political agreement was signed.

- Berat. One of Albania's oldest towns, where rioting broke out in January over lost savings in pyramid schemes. Reports suggest that rebels tried to seize control of the town at the weekend. A military airport lies between Berat and Kucove, 10 km (six miles) further north, where rebels have also been active.
